trimebutine-200mg-jeong.refEnHtml:
Over-the-counterRegulates gut movement

Trimebutine Maleate 200 mg TabletA digestive aid that regulates gut movement

Trimebutine maleate 200 mg

This medicine is used for acid reflux and hiatal hernia; for the digestive problems that come with gastritis, duodenitis or ulcers — stomach pain, indigestion, nausea and vomiting; and for irritable bowel syndrome and spastic colon.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter

Ingredient

Trimebutine maleate 200 mg

How it works

Regulates gut movement

Main symptoms

Stomach pain, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, irritable bowel symptoms

Who should be careful

Inherited lactose metabolism disorders; pregnancy and breastfeeding

Why this one

A digestive aid that regulates gut movement

How to take it

Adults take 100–200 mg three times a day, before meals. The dose may be adjusted to suit your age and symptoms.

Before you take this

  • Do not take this if you have an inherited problem with lactose metabolism, such as galactose intolerance.
  • Talk to a pharmacist before taking it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or if you have ever reacted to Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).

mecobalamin-500ug-capsule.refEnHtml:
Over-the-counterSupplies vitamin B12 (for nerves)

Mecobalamin 500 ㎍ CapsuleA vitamin B12 preparation that acts on peripheral nerves

Mecobalamin 500 ㎍

This medicine is used for peripheral neuropathy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter

Ingredient

Mecobalamin 500 ㎍

How it works

Supplies vitamin B12 (for nerves)

Main symptoms

Peripheral neuropathy such as tingling in the hands and feet

Who should be careful

Seek advice if there is no improvement after one month

Why this one

A vitamin B12 preparation that acts on peripheral nerves

How to take it

Adults take three capsules (1,500 ㎍) a day, divided into three doses.

Before you take this

  • Do not take this if you have ever reacted to this medicine or if you have an inherited problem with lactose metabolism.
  • Talk to a pharmacist before taking it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, and seek advice if there is no improvement or it gets worse after about one month.

Dexpanthenol 100 mg TabletA preparation used as a supportive treatment for hair loss

Dexpanthenol 100 mg

This medicine is used as a supportive treatment for hair loss.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter

Ingredient

Dexpanthenol 100 mg

How it works

Supports treatment for hair loss

Main symptoms

Hair loss

Who should be careful

Under 19; not for any purpose other than hair loss

Why this one

A preparation used as a supportive treatment for hair loss

How to take it

Adults take one tablet three times a day. The treatment period is 6 weeks.

Before you take this

  • Do not take this if you have ever reacted to it, if you are under 19, for any purpose other than hair loss, or if you have an inherited condition such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
  • Talk to a pharmacist before taking it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have ever had a drug allergy.
  • If there is no improvement after about 6 weeks, stop taking it.

folic-acid-1mg-jeong.refEnHtml:
Over-the-counterSupplies folic acid (folate)

Folic Acid 1 mg TabletA vitamin preparation that replaces folate

Folic acid 1 mg

This medicine is used to prevent and treat folic acid deficiency, to supply folic acid during pregnancy and breastfeeding, and for anaemia linked to folic acid deficiency — such as anaemia from poor nutrition, anaemia in pregnancy, and anaemia in children.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter

Ingredient

Folic acid 1 mg

How it works

Supplies folic acid (folate)

Main symptoms

Folic acid deficiency; folic acid supply in pregnancy and breastfeeding; anaemia from poor nutrition

Who should be careful

Pernicious anaemia from vitamin B12 deficiency

Why this one

A vitamin preparation that replaces folate

How to take it

To treat folic acid deficiency, adults and children 24 months or older take 0.25–1 mg a day. To prevent it, or when the body needs more, take 0.1–0.25 mg a day.

Before you take this

  • Do not take this if you have ever reacted to it, or if you have pernicious anaemia or megaloblastic anaemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency (it can mask the cause of the anaemia), or if you have an inherited condition such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
  • Talk to a pharmacist before taking it if you are taking a folate-metabolism inhibitor such as methotrexate or trimethoprim, an anti-epileptic such as phenytoin, sulfasalazine or cholestyramine, or if you are under a doctor's care.
  • If there is no improvement after about a month, stop taking it.
